summary: Build citizen-centred design skills, service blueprints, and improvement roadmaps. Book digital service standards training with TrainingCred.
lede: Digital service standards and citizen-centred design bring user research and service design methods together to improve public-facing digital journeys. For professionals who shape, manage or assess digital public services, the course builds practical skills in journey mapping and service blueprinting to identify friction and plan improvements. It also covers accessibility reviews, prototyping and KPI reporting to help teams assess services and communicate priorities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, redesign, govern, or measure digital public services and citizen-facing journeys. Service Designers responsible for citizen journey mapping and service blueprinting. Public Sector Product Owners managing digital service priorities and backlog decisions. Government UX Researchers conducting user interviews, testing, and insight synthesis. Digital Transformation Managers coordinating service redesign across departments and channels. Policy Leads aligning service design choices with public value and delivery constraints. Programme Managers tracking service improvement milestones and governance actions. Service Delivery Managers reducing friction in citizen-facing operational processes. Accessibility Specialists reviewing service journeys against inclusive design requirements. Citizen Experience Leads turning feedback into measurable service improvements. Business Analysts documenting process gaps and future-state service requirements.
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of public-service operations, digital service delivery, or service improvement work. Familiarity with basic process mapping, stakeholder coordination, and common service performance measures is helpful. No coding is required, but you should be prepared to review service journeys, interpret user feedback, and work on practical design exercises using templates and workshop outputs.
